title: The Unofficial Scholarship
premise: Kestrel Whitlock transfers to Hollowmere Academy on a scholarship he never applied for, counting down 180 days until graduation. When the school's legendary ghost, the Cartographer, begins leaving him notes written in ink that shouldn't exist — ink that remembers things Kestrel has forgotten — he discovers the 'scholarship' is a bargain struck before his birth: a life traded for a debt. To survive the year, Kestrel must win both the school's beloved Founders' Cup championship and the invisible contest beneath it, a memory-for-memory game against the ghost's other chosen heirs. In the end, Kestrel wins by refusing to play: he gives back the stolen memories that made him 'special,' choosing an ordinary, self-authored identity over survival by inheritance — and frees the Cartographer, who was the first student ever erased.
about_author: Freya Delacroix is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent three years cataloguing a century of student letters and never found one signed in disappearing ink. She writes young adult fiction about institutions that remember too much and teenagers who remember too little.

chapters.title: One Hundred Eighty Days
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He arrives at Hollowmere Academy mid-winter, resentful of the full-ride scholarship no one can explain, and starts chalking days off his dorm wall. Emotional beat: guarded numbness; he treats school as a sentence to serve, establishing his transactional view of survival.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Knows the Rules
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Scholarship student Marisol Vega warns him about the Cartographer, the ghost said to map what students lose, and shows him a door in the library that isn't on any floor plan. Beat: wary curiosity; first crack in Kestrel's isolation as someone offers help unprompted.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He finds the first note tucked into his locker — his name, then a fact only his dead mother could know, written in ink that shifts color when he blinks. Beat: fear braided with longing; grief reopens where he'd sealed it.

chapters.title: Tryouts for a Trophy Nobody Cares About
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Pressured to join the quiz-and-endurance team competing for the Founders' Cup, he meets rival heir Theodore Ashcombe, who is too polished and too interested in Kestrel's notes. Beat: reluctant belonging; the championship becomes cover for something stranger.

chapters.title: What the Basement Remembers
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She leads Kestrel below the old wing, where the school was built over a demolished orphanage, and the walls sweat ink after midnight. Beat: dread deepening into resolve; the school's foundation is literally built on erased children.

chapters.title: The Second Note
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A note describes a memory Kestrel doesn't have — standing in snow at age six — and when he touches the paper, the scene floods back whole. Beat: vertigo and hunger; recovered memory feels like being handed pieces of himself, and he wants more.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Offer
chapters.summary: Theodore's POV. He reveals there are four heirs in the Cartographer's game, each trading memories for advantages, and offers Kestrel an alliance. Beat: seduction and suspicion; Theodore is charming, wounded, and clearly losing something he can't name.

chapters.title: Founders' Cup, Round One
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The team survives the first trial using a memory Kestrel didn't know he had — and afterward he can't recall his mother's voice anymore. Beat: triumph curdling into horror; every win costs him something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Self
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Terrified, he writes down everything he knows about himself and hides the list, discovering gaps already: a summer, a friend, a reason he flinches at bells. Beat: quiet panic; identity revealed as fragile, editable, and already edited.

chapters.title: The Third Heir Quits
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Heir Priya Chandrasekaran tries to walk away from the game and wakes up unable to remember her own brother — proof that quitting forfeits everything anyway. Beat: despair; the rules are a trap with no legal exit.

chapters.title: Down the Unmapped Stair
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the notes' accumulating clues, he finds the Cartographer's study behind the impossible door: walls of maps charting every memory ever taken at Hollowmere. Beat: awe tipping into anger; his whole life has been plotted here since before he could read.

chapters.title: The Bargain Before Birth
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV (fragmented). The ghost reveals the truth: Kestrel's parents traded his earliest years for his survival during the fire at the orphanage site — and the debt comes due at graduation. Beat: devastating clarity; Kestrel learns he is collateral, not a beneficiary.

chapters.title: Round Three, Empty Handed
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Competing with deliberately surrendered memories, Kestrel loses badly while Ashcombe soars — and Ashcombe's eyes have gone flat and gray. Beat: humiliation reframed as insight; winning the game means ceasing to be anyone.

chapters.title: Marisol's Confession
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She admits she was the Cartographer's first chosen heir twenty years ago, escaped by hiding inside her own forgetting, and has been guiding Kestrel toward the same trick. Beat: betrayal transformed into trust; her help was always self-interested and still real.

chapters.title: The Fourth Heir
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The final heir is revealed: Headmaster Lorne, who has been renewing his own bargain for forty years and needs a fresh soul to retire his debt. Beat: cold fury; the institution itself is the predator, wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Everything I Wrote Down
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. His hidden inventory list is confiscated, and reading it back he can't feel half of it — the words are true but hollow. Beat: grief at its lowest point; he mourns himself while still alive.

chapters.title: The Map With a Hole In It
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Studying the Cartographer's master map, they find one unmapped space: the moment of the original trade, where the ghost's own name should be. Beat: dawning hope; the system has a blind spot, and it's shaped like mercy.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Lorne offers Kestrel freedom in exchange for taking Marisol's place; Ashcombe, nearly empty, begs Kestrel to just take the deal. Beat: moral crucible; Kestrel must choose between survival, loyalty, and principle with dawn hours away.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the final Founders' Cup trial, held atop the old orphanage foundations, Kestrel deliberately loses — then invokes the unmapped clause, offering back every traded memory including his mother's sacrifice. Beat: climax; surrender as victory, breaking the game's logic open.

chapters.title: Ink Runs Dry
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV (clarifying). Unbound by Kestrel's refusal, the ghost remembers his own name — Tomas, first erased student — and turns the ledger on Lorne, who collapses into the nothing he dealt others. Beat: cathartic reckoning; the predator is consumed by its own accounting.

chapters.title: One Hundred Eighty Days, Later
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ordinary now, scholarship explained as a mundane endowment, Kestrel graduates remembering less but owning all of it; he and Marisol plant a tree over the foundations. Beat: bittersweet peace; identity rebuilt from choice rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: A Note, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. On the last day, Kestrel finds one final note in his locker — not a demand, just his name in fading ink and the word 'yours.' Beat: gentle closure with an open door; some memories choose to stay given, not taken.
